title: Making Generative AI Workable at Work: Accountability, Localization, and Representation in Kenyan and Nigerian Small Businesses

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative analysis of semi-structured interviews with SMB workers in Kenya and Nigeria, documenting 'locality gaps' where AI outputs default to Western/Americanized assumptions and fail to integrate local institutional, legal, and culturally specific knowledge.

Analyzing interview accounts and user demonstrations to identify breakdowns where generative AI tools fail to accurately process, recognize, or generate local African languages, place names, code-mixing, and accents in text and speech interfaces.

Collecting qualitative accounts and artifact demonstrations from users of text-to-image and voice cloning tools to document visual and auditory representational failures, such as visually incoherent depictions of Black individuals, misrepresentations of African landscapes, and the lack of authentic African synthetic voices.
